examples.title: Alien Armada
examples.summary: Hold back a marching armada before it lands. Hide behind the shields, and pick off the mystery ship for a bonus.
examples.controls: Left and right move your base. Fire shoots.
highlights: The armada is made of characters, so it moves a whole character, 8 pixels, at a time.
A shot hits when the screen cell under its tip holds an alien character.
The score adds up in decimal, using the 6502's BCD mode (SED).
tryThis: Redraw the aliens: their pixels are under ALIEN CHARACTERS.

examples.title: Rockfall
examples.summary: Dig through four caves, grab enough gems to open the exit and get out before time runs out. Boulders fall, fireflies roam.
examples.controls: Move to dig. Hold fire and push a direction to grab without stepping.
highlights: The screen is the map: the caves live in screen memory and nowhere else.
Every tile that moves has bit 7 set, so one BMI finds it and a jump table moves it.
The caves are drawn as plain text at the end of the file.
tryThis: Design your own cave in CAVES.
Speed the game up: lower TICK_FRAMES (down to 2).

examples.title: Jumpin' Jo
examples.style: Super Mario Bros. and The Great Giana Sisters, 1985-87
examples.summary: Run and jump across two smoothly scrolling levels. Stomp the bugs, bash blocks for gems and reach the flag.
examples.controls: Left and right run. Up or fire jumps; hold it to jump higher.
highlights: Smooth scrolling: $D016 slides the screen, and an unrolled loop shifts it every 8 pixels.
A raster split keeps the status line still above the scrolling level.
Speeds in 1/256ths of a pixel make the jumps rise and fall smoothly.
tryThis: Build your own level in LEVELS.

examples.title: Nova Strike
examples.summary: Fly through an endless alien cave, blast waves of enemies and charge your beam for the guardian at the end of each stage.
examples.controls: Fly in any direction. Tap fire to shoot; hold it to charge the beam.
highlights: The cave is never stored: each column is invented as it scrolls in.
Enemy waves are rows in a table: when, what, how many, where.
The beam and the guardian are sprites stretched with $D01D and $D017.
tryThis: Design your own attack waves in WAVES.

examples.title: Dojo Duel
examples.summary: A karate contest at sunset. Block, duck and strike to score three points first, then face an opponent with a higher belt.
examples.controls: Fire punches. Fire with towards kicks, with up high-kicks, with down sweeps. Up blocks, down ducks.
highlights: One raster interrupt runs 17 times a frame to paint the sunset a text row at a time.
The fighters facing left are made at the start by mirroring the sprites facing right.
Moves are rows in a table, and the opponent's skill comes from tables indexed by its belt.
tryThis: Face a black belt from the start: set START_BELT to 6.
Paint a different sky in BAND_COLORS.
